tips.imageStaging: Stages a whole room from one photo: pick a room type and a furniture style and the AI furnishes it. Best for empty or nearly empty rooms when you want a fast, complete result.
tips.basicMask: Paint over one part of a photo, then describe the change you want. Best for small fixes (swap a sofa, clear a countertop) when the rest of the shot is already right.
tips.pdfTo3d: Chat with an AI designer that stages, redesigns and keeps iterating on a room with you. Best when you are exploring looks rather than finishing one photo. Desktop only.
tips.maskingStudio: Highlight several areas in different colors and give each its own furniture photo or prompt, then stage them all at once. Best when you need exact control, since everything outside your highlights stays pixel-perfect.
tips.exteriorStudio: Cleans up an exterior photo of a property: change the time of day, clear the sky, and remove parked cars and clutter. Best for the front elevation, yard and street shots, the ones the staging tools deliberately never touch.

basics.label: Basics
basics.question: What is virtual staging?
basics.answer: Virtual staging digitally furnishes a photo of an empty or dated room so buyers can see what the space could become. Nothing structural changes: the walls, windows, floors and proportions stay exactly as photographed, and only furniture and decor are added. It does the same job traditional staging does with a moving truck, in seconds instead of weeks. It is now standard practice on listings that would otherwise photograph as empty boxes.

turnaround.label: Turnaround
turnaround.question: How fast is it?
turnaround.answer: About 8 seconds per photo. Complex rooms and heavily detailed styles can take a little longer, but you are waiting seconds, not days, which is long enough to try three styles on the same room while you decide which one sells it. There is no queue, no booking and no back-and-forth with a stager: you upload, pick a look, and download.

pricing.label: Pricing
pricing.question: What does it cost?
pricing.answer: You can stage for free, with no card. Stagify+ is $11.99 a month and unlocks the higher-quality image model, multiple variations per render, furniture removal, the Masking Studio and the AI Designer. For teams there is Enterprise: everyone on your company email is covered automatically, and you pay per generation instead of per seat. For comparison, physically staging a home usually runs $2,000 to $5,000.

studios.label: The Studios
studios.question: What else can Stagify do?
studios.answer: Quite a lot. The AI Designer redesigns a whole room conversationally, so you can ask for a warmer palette or a bigger sofa and keep refining. The Masking Studio gives pixel-level control over which areas may change. The Exterior Studio works on curb appeal rather than interiors. The Listing Studio takes a whole set of photos through in one pass and produces a link you can send a seller for sign-off. Everything you make lands in your gallery.

control.label: Control
control.question: How much control do I have over the result?
control.answer: As much as you want. Pick a preset style and you are done in one click. Choose “Custom” and you can describe the look in your own words. Open the Masking Studio and you can paint exactly which parts of the photo are allowed to change, attaching specific furniture to each area, so anything you did not select stays untouched. The AI Designer sits in between: describe what you want changed, look at the result, and refine it in conversation.

photos.label: Photos
photos.question: What kind of photo works best?
photos.answer: Wide, bright and level. Shoot from a corner so two walls and plenty of floor are visible, keep the camera roughly chest height, and let in as much natural light as you can. Empty or lightly furnished rooms give the AI the cleanest canvas, though Stagify+ can remove existing furniture first. Avoid tight crops, heavy fisheye distortion, and photos where the floor is barely in frame, since there is nowhere to place furniture convincingly.

disclosure.label: Disclosure
disclosure.question: Can I use these photos in an MLS listing?
disclosure.answer: Yes, and virtual staging is standard practice, but disclose it. Most MLSs and local rules ask that a digitally furnished photo be labeled as such, usually in the caption. Stagify can stamp “Virtually staged” onto the image for you, on any plan. Because only furniture and decor change, and never the structure of the room, the photo stays an honest representation of the space. Check your own board for the exact wording it expects.

privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.question: What happens to the photos I upload?
privacy.answer: They travel over an encrypted connection, get processed, and are not kept permanently on our servers. Renders you save go to your own gallery, which only you can see unless you share a link. We do not sell personal information, and you keep ownership of both your uploads and the images Stagify generates. We share data only with the providers needed to run the service, such as the AI and payment processors, which the Privacy Policy lists.

whyStagify.label: Why Stagify
whyStagify.question: How is this different from other tools?
whyStagify.answer: Most tools do one of three things well. Stagify does all three: it is cheap enough to stage on a whim, conversational enough to redesign a room rather than merely decorate it, and precise enough to control the result pixel by pixel. Add the exterior and whole-listing workflows, eleven languages, full copyright on everything you generate, and no ads or per-image fees, and you get a tool you can use on every listing instead of saving for the hero shot.

techHelp.subtitle: Most problems have a quick fix. Find your issue below, and if you’re still stuck, our team is one email away.

i1.a: Make sure the file is a JPG, PNG, WebP, or HEIC under 25 MB. Very large phone photos sometimes fail. Resize the image or take a screenshot of it, then upload again. If it still fails, refresh the page and retry.

i2.a: Use a clear, well-lit photo taken straight-on, with the whole room visible and minimal clutter. Blurry, dark, or extreme wide-angle shots produce weaker results. New here? Watch the step-by-step walkthrough first.

i1.q: How do I get the most realistic staging?
i1.a: Shoot the room straight-on in daylight with the whole space in frame and surfaces cleared. Pick the exact room type and style before you generate, then create two or three variations and keep the strongest. Open the staging studio to try it.

i2.q: Which plan or tool should I use?
i2.a: Free is perfect for quick one-off rooms. Stagify+ unlocks unlimited generations, higher-quality models, the masking tool and the Prompt Bar. AI Designer redesigns an entire room from a short chat, which is best when you want it to make the decisions for you.

i3.q: Can I control the furniture and layout?
i3.a: Yes. With Stagify+ the Prompt Bar lets you describe specifics like “add a sectional sofa and a large area rug,” and the Furniture tool brings in your own pieces. If just one area looks off, mask it and regenerate only that spot instead of redoing the whole image.

masking.title: Stage with exact precision
masking.subtitle: In the new Masking Studio, highlight the areas to restage, add your own furniture, and everything else stays pixel-perfect. (Stagify+ Exclusive)

i4.q: How do I stage several areas at once?
i4.a: With Stagify+ the Masking Studio lets you highlight up to six areas in different colors, give each one its own furniture photo or prompt, and stage them all in parallel. Only the highlighted spots can change, and every area can generate several versions so you keep the best one.

i1.q: My generation is stuck or taking too long.
i1.a: Most images finish in about 8 seconds, but a Stagify+ render with several variations, or one where the AI retries for a better result, can legitimately take longer. Leave it running. You can press Cancel under the progress bar at any time, and if something has genuinely gone wrong we stop it for you and say so. Avoid switching tabs or locking your phone while it runs.

i2.q: The result has odd furniture or artifacts.
i2.a: AI staging isn’t perfect on every pass. Generate again for a new variation, switch to a different style, or use the masking tool to fix only the area that looks off instead of redoing the whole image.

i3.q: Nothing changed or the room still looks empty.
i3.a: This usually means a room type or style wasn’t selected, or the photo was too dark for the model to read. Pick a room type and style, then try a brighter photo. Want the AI to handle it end-to-end? Try AI Designer.

i1.a: Check your spam or promotions folder. Codes can take a minute. If it still hasn’t come, use “Resend code” and make sure your email is typed correctly.

i2.a: On the sign-in screen choose “Forgot your password?” and we’ll email you a reset link. The link expires after one hour.

i3.a: Allow pop-ups for stagify.ai and make sure third-party cookies aren’t fully blocked, then try again. You can also sign in with your email and password instead.

i1.q: How do I manage or cancel Stagify+?
i1.a: Click the profile icon in the top right, then tap the Stripe icon next to Stagify+ to open your billing dashboard, where you can update or cancel your subscription. You can also open the Stripe billing portal directly. You keep access until the end of the current billing period.

i2.q: I was charged but don’t see Stagify+ features.
i2.a: Sign out and back in to refresh your account. If the features still don’t appear, email us at team@stagify.ai from the address you used.

i1.a: Use an up-to-date version of Chrome, Safari, Edge, or Firefox. Older browsers may not support the editor or the drag-to-compare tools.

i2.q: The page is slow or buttons don’t respond.
i2.a: Hard-refresh the page (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + R) to clear a stale version, close unused tabs, and disable ad blockers for stagify.ai, which can interfere with uploads.

i3.q: The site won’t load at all.
i3.a: Check your internet connection, then try a private/incognito window. If it loads there, clear your browser cache for stagify.ai.

tips.gallery: Saved renders stay in your account, so you can reopen them, download them again, or send a client a share link. A free gallery holds only your most recent rooms and drops the oldest as new ones arrive. On Stagify+ nothing is ever evicted.
tips.customizable: Choose the room type and the furniture style before you generate, so a nursery doesn’t come back as a home office and a coastal brief doesn’t come back mid-century. The full set of rooms and styles is on both plans.
tips.fastModel: The default generator, tuned for turnaround. It comes back in seconds, which is what you want while you are still trying room types and styles against each other. Available on every plan.
tips.unlimited: Stage as many photos as you like. There are no credits to buy and no per-render charge on either plan. Stagify+ changes what a generation can do, not how many of them you get.
tips.hqModel: A slower, more careful generator for the frame that actually goes on the listing. It holds straight lines, window light and reflections together far better, so the furniture sits in the room instead of on top of it.
tips.remove: Tick one box and the room is emptied first: sofas, clutter, wall art, all of it. Then it is restaged from a clean slate. This is the one you need for an occupied listing, where staging on top of the seller’s furniture never looks right.
tips.designer: A chat window with your photo in it. Ask for what you want in plain language, then keep refining the same image over several turns. Warmer wood, lose the rug, try it as a nursery. No need to start a fresh render each time.
tips.masking: Paint over part of a result and change only that. Everything outside the brush stays untouched, pixel for pixel, so you can swap a single chair or repaint one wall without re-rolling the whole room.
tips.studio: The full version of masking. Mark several areas in different colors, give each one its own brief or its own furniture photo, and stage them all in a single pass. Then generate a few options per area and keep the best of each.
tips.exterior: For the shot every listing opens with. Change the time of day, clear a flat grey sky and take out parked cars and bins, while the property itself stays exactly as photographed.
tips.variations: Ask for several takes on the same brief in one go. They differ in layout and furniture choice rather than being the same render twice, so you have something to choose between instead of re-rolling until one lands.
tips.references: Upload a product photo of an actual sofa, bed or dining set, and the room is staged with that piece rather than something generically similar. Useful when a client, a builder or a stager has already chosen the furniture.
